answer: Picture each new agent as a cedar sapling: before its votes count, it must lock a refundable bond and survive ninety days of peer review, gaining weight only as honest work accumulates. A forger who wants a grove of fake identities must tie up capital for every seedling and wait months, while any clone caught colluding forfeits its stake. Public funding logs act as a lantern, letting peers trace accounts bankrolled by one wallet and slash them together.
